evidence.positive: Pointed both Epic tenants at a local mock Epic FHIR R4 server (tenants.mayo.fhir-r4-server-base-url / tenants.mgb.fhir.r4-url plus a mock oauth2/token endpoint and a self-signed epic.oauth key pair, injected as -D flags in the container entrypoint; the DB tenant rows confirmed the override: mayo-mayo -> http://host.docker.internal:8899/mayo/R4) and drove the real commands through POST /api/admin/integration-harness/{tenant}/GET_OBSERVATIONS_LATEST and GET_OBSERVATIONS_LAST_24_HRS as admin. Mayo latest-observations returned EGFR='<15' mL/min/1.73m2 (Quantity with a '<' comparator), GLUCOSE='60-70' mg/dL (valueRange), PTT='1:16' (valueRatio), POTASSIUM='4.2' mmol/L (valueString split); Mayo last-24-hrs labs returned the same four. MGB latest-observations returned CREATININE='1-5' mg/dL (valueRange), POTASSIUM='4.2:1' mmol/L (valueRatio, unit composed from numerator/denominator), BODY_HEIGHT='>180' cm (comparator kept), BODY_WEIGHT='70.5' kg (valueString). A second payload confirmed the ticket's exact example and the preserved CodeableConcept path: MGB CREATININE='>1.0-5.0' with no unit, Mayo EGFR='>90' with no unit, PREGNANCY_STATUS='Pregnant' on both tenants. Separately, a demo patient seeded with GESTATIONAL_AGE_BIRTH='252-266' d returned HTTP 200 from GET /api/admin/patients/PMRN-GA-1/insulin-daily-dose with the log line 'Non-numeric value for GESTATIONAL_AGE_BIRTH: 252-266'.
evidence.negative: Flipped the mock payload to values that must NOT reach a record and re-ran both tenants. Both returned HTTP 200 with data {} (no observations) and no exception. App log named the refusal and the FHIR type for each: 'Observation urn:uuid:mgb-creat-ratio-nodenom has no value - CREATININE - Ratio', 'urn:uuid:mgb-k-range-nounits has no units - POTASSIUM - 3.5-5 Range', 'urn:uuid:mgb-height-range-inches does not match preferred units (cm) - BODY_HEIGHT - 70-72 in', 'urn:uuid:mgb-weight-cancelled has non-result status CANCELLED - BODY_WEIGHT', and on Mayo 'urn:uuid:mayo-egfr-range-empty has no value for EGFR', 'urn:uuid:mayo-k-ratio-nodenom has no value for POTASSIUM', 'urn:uuid:mayo-glucose-cancelled has invalid status CANCELLED for GLUCOSE', 'urn:uuid:mayo-qtc-preliminary has invalid status PRELIMINARY for QTC_INTERVAL', 'urn:uuid:mayo-weight-range-lb preferred units mismatch (kg)'. So a Ratio missing a side, a unitless Range where units are required, a wrong-unit Range and a canceled or unreviewed result are each refused with a stated reason instead of landing as a value.
evidence.red_check: Two swaps, both reverted and both verified. (1) Compiled the parent commit's FhirUtils (19677313d^, @Slf4j replaced with an explicit logger) inside the container against /app/jib-classpath-file and dropped it into /app/classes, which precedes /app/libs on the jib classpath, so it shadowed client-integration-api-0.1.96-SNAPSHOT.jar. After restart, the same Mayo positive payload went red: EGFR came back as '15' with the '<' silently dropped (a rule would have acted on 15), and GLUCOSE and PTT vanished from the result with 'Observation urn:uuid:mayo-glucose-range has no value for GLUCOSE' and 'Observation urn:uuid:mayo-ptt-ratio has no value for PTT' in the log - lines that appear exactly once in the whole container log, at 18:54:49, only while the pre-fix class was loaded. (2) Compiled the parent commit's Calculator the same way; GET /api/admin/patients/PMRN-GA-1/insulin-daily-dose then returned HTTP 500 with 'java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Float.intValue()" because the return value of "...Observation.getNumericObservationValue()" is null' at Calculator.gestationalAgeObservationToDays, where the shipped build returns 200 and a warning. Both class files were deleted, 'diff -r /tmp/classes-backup /app/classes' reported identical, and after restart the positive Mayo/MGB results and the 200 on insulin-daily-dose were confirmed restored. The container entrypoint was then restored from /app/entrypoint.sh.orig and the app restarted clean.

red_check_signature: urn:uuid:mayo-ptt-ratio has no value for PTT
caveats: Epic was a local mock serving crafted R4 bundles; no real Epic August-2026 payload was observed, and OAuth was satisfied with a self-signed key against the mock token endpoint.

MGBGetLatestObservationR4Command (creatinine/potassium) and MGBGetPediatricObservationsR4Command are only reachable through MGB patient-info retrieval, which no endpoint in this instance can drive, so those two call sites rest on their unit tests alone.
The inpatient/outpatient blood-pressure component commands were also not reachable at runtime here (MGB vital signs disabled), so their guard refactor is unit-tested only.

'Never becomes a number downstream' was verified at the observation-record boundary - the value keeps its prefix and getNumericObservationValue is a plain Float.parseFloat over it - but no rule was evaluated on a comparator value at runtime.

Behavior change worth a reviewer's eye: MGB latest-observations now stores a narrative string as the value where the quantity-only filter used to drop it (observed CREATININE='SEE COMMENT' with no unit). ValueUnit.fromStrings keeps it out of Patient.creatinine, but it will show wherever the raw observation value is displayed.

MGBGetQTCIntervalR4Command still accepts only valueQuantity and drops any other type with no log line; QTc was not in the ticket's exposure list, so this is a follow-up rather than a defect in this change.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage added with the fix is thorough and I would not duplicate it: FhirUtilsTest covers every value type, every comparator, one-sided and unbounded Ranges, Ratios missing a side, narrative and multi-line strings, CodeableConcept and the status helper; the Mayo and MGB latest/labs/single/pediatric command tests each cover Range, Ratio, comparator, unit-mismatch and canceled-result refusals; CalculatorGestationalAgeTest and MGBBloodPressureComponentValueR4Test cover the two crash guards. The gaps are one level up: every test builds HAPI objects in memory, so nothing asserts the extraction against a parsed Epic-shaped JSON payload, and the QTc command's quantity-only filter has no test stating what it does with the new types.
proposed_tests: FhirUtils extraction driven from a parsed Epic-shaped R4 JSON bundle fixture (valueQuantity with comparator, valueRange, valueRatio, comparator-prefixed valueString) rather than hand-built HAPI objects, so a payload-shape surprise is caught.
MGBGetQTCIntervalR4Command: assert current behavior for a Range/Ratio/String-valued QTc and that the refusal is logged, or extend it to the shared extraction first.
MGB latest-observations: lock in that a narrative valueString now reaches CREATININE, so the widened filter is a deliberate assertion rather than a side effect.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Both Epic tenants were pointed at a mock Epic FHIR R4 server and the observation commands were run through the admin integration harness, which returned Range, Ratio, comparator-Quantity and String values each with the right value and unit, including >1.0-5.0 kept whole.
Negative: With a Ratio missing a side, a unitless Range, a wrong-unit Range and a canceled result, both tenants returned no observations and logged a refusal naming the FHIR type instead of storing a value.
Red check: The parent commit's FhirUtils was compiled and swapped into the running container, which dropped the comparator (<15 read as 15) and lost the Range and Ratio values entirely, and the parent commit's Calculator turned the same gestational-age request into a 500; both were removed and the shipped behavior confirmed restored.

Automation: Unit coverage added with the fix is thorough, so the proposals are a JSON-payload-level extraction test and coverage of the QTc command, which still reads valueQuantity only.
